mainTopic: מחמר בשבת (driving a loaded animal on שבת): Can someone get סקילה for doing it on purpose even though there is no חטאת for doing it by mistake?
overview: This amud is about a מחמר, someone who drives a loaded animal on שבת. According to רב זביד, רמי בר חמא rules that a מחמר who acts by mistake brings no חטאת, but one who acts on purpose gets סקילה. רבא objects from a ברייתא that seems to say that without a חטאת there is no סקילה. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא only works in one direction, so מחמר can be an exception. Next, the גמרא introduces another teacher, רבא, the brother (or father) of רב מרי בר רחל. First it stops for a side question about family lineage, and it answers by suggesting there were two men with that name. This teacher then reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that a מחמר is פטור מכלום, free of every punishment. There is no חטאת, because all of the Torah is compared to עבודה זרה. There is no סקילה, because without a חטאת there is no סקילה. There are no lashes, because the שבת לאו is a warning for מיתת בית דין.

steps.title: רב זביד's version of רמי בר חמא's ruling on driving an animal
steps.stepSummary: According to רב זביד, רמי בר חמא rules that a מחמר on שבת brings no חטאת if he acted by mistake, but gets סקילה if he acted on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד taught it this way: רמי בר חמא said: One who drives a loaded animal on שבת brings no sin-offering if he did it by mistake. If he did it on purpose, he is liable to stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב זביד's version of a ruling by רמי בר חמא about someone who drives his loaded animal on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the punishment for doing something on purpose and the offering for doing it by mistake go together. Here רמי בר חמא splits them: by mistake there is no חטאת, but on purpose there is full סקילה. This unusual split is what the rest of the sugya argues about.

keyTerms.meaning: taught it this way (introduces a different version of a teaching)
one who drives a loaded animal from behind
sin-offering brought for a mistaken sin
stoning, the death penalty for knowingly breaking שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a case where the usual link between חטאת and סקילה breaks.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid taught it this way:
Rami bar Chama said:
One who drives behind a loaded animal on Shabbat,
if by mistake, he is not liable to a sin-offering;
if on purpose, he is liable to stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an alternate version of רמי בר חמא's teaching, which continues from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחמר: by mistake there is no חטאת; on purpose there is סקילה.

steps.title: רבא objects from a ברייתא linking sin-offering and stoning
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: whatever brings a חטאת by mistake brings סקילה on purpose. He reads into it that if there is no חטאת, there is no סקילה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: 'One who breaks שבת with an act that brings a sin-offering when done by mistake is liable to stoning when done on purpose.' This implies that if an act does not bring a sin-offering by mistake, it does not bring stoning on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רמי בר חמא from a ברייתא that seems to say סקילה only applies where there would also be a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly says only one thing: חטאת by mistake means סקילה on purpose. רבא draws an inference (a דיוק) from it: no חטאת by mistake means no סקילה on purpose. Since מחמר has no חטאת, this inference would rule out סקילה and contradict רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'this implies…', the opening of an inference

steps.confusionAlert: The second half, beginning 'הא אין חייבין', is not written in the ברייתא. It is רבא's own inference from what the ברייתא says.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
One who desecrates Shabbat
with something for whose mistaken doing one is liable to a sin-offering,
is liable to stoning for doing it on purpose.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין חַיָּיבִין עַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת —
phrases.english: This implies: where one is not liable to a sin-offering for the mistake,
one is not liable to stoning for doing it on purpose!

steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's ruling that a מחמר who acts on purpose gets סקילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A דיוק from the ברייתא says that without חטאת there is no סקילה. מחמר has no חטאת, so it should have no סקילה.

steps.title: The ברייתא never says the reverse, so driving is an exception
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. The ברייתא only says that חטאת leads to סקילה. There can still be cases with סקילה and no חטאת, and מחמר is one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the ברייתא actually say 'but where one is not liable…'? This is what it means: something that brings a sin-offering by mistake brings stoning on purpose. And there is also something that brings no sin-offering by mistake but does bring stoning on purpose. What is it? Driving a loaded animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רמי בר חמא by showing that the ברייתא does not actually say what רבא inferred from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'If A then B' does not mean 'if not A then not B.' The ברייתא only promises that every act with חטאת also has סקילה. It leaves room for an act with סקילה and no חטאת, and the גמרא names מחמר as that case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Does it actually say…?', which rejects a claimed reading
'This is what it means', which offers the correct reading

steps.whatToRemember: מחמר is an exception: there is no חטאת by mistake, yet there is סקילה on purpose. The ברייתא only works in one direction.

phrases.english: Does it actually teach 'but where one is not liable, etc.'?
This is what it is saying:
Something for whose mistaken doing one is liable to a sin-offering,
one is liable to stoning for doing it on purpose.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין עַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת —
phrases.english: And there is something for whose mistaken doing one is not liable to a sin-offering,
yet one is liable to stoning for doing it on purpose.
And what is it? Driving a loaded animal.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the claimed inference is rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא sets up a two-way rule: no חטאת means no סקילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only goes one way. מחמר is an exception, with סקילה but no חטאת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רמי בר חמא's ruling stands, as רב זביד reports it.

steps.title: Introducing רבא, brother or father of רב מרי בר רחל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to bring another opinion about מחמר, from רבא, who was either the brother or the father of רב מרי בר רחל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא, the brother of רב מרי בר רחל, and some say the father of רב מרי בר רחל…
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It names the next speaker on the topic of מחמר, but before he speaks, the גמרא stops for a side question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of how this רבא was related to רב מרי בר רחל: brother or father. The next steps only discuss the second version. רבא's actual ruling on מחמר comes after this side discussion.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל,
phrases.english: Rava, the brother of Rav Mari bar Rachel,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל.
phrases.english: and some say the father of Rav Mari bar Rachel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a different opinion on מחמר, which the side question then interrupts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An attribution only. The ruling itself comes later.

steps.title: If רבא was his father, why did רב need to validate him?
steps.stepSummary: On the 'father' version there is a difficulty. רב had to confirm רב מרי בר רחל's status before appointing him an official of בבל, which shows his father was a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the second version, there is a difficulty with the fact that רב validated רב מרי בר רחל and appointed him as an official of בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the version that calls רבא the father of רב מרי בר רחל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had to validate רב מרי בר רחל through his Jewish mother, רחל. That only makes sense if his father was not Jewish. A non-Jew could not be a חכם named רבא, so the 'father' version looks impossible.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a side question about family history. It is not about the laws of מחמר.

phrases.english: According to the latter version, it is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַב אַכְשְׁרֵיהּ לְרַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל
phrases.english: that which Rav validated Rav Mari bar Rachel
and appointed him among the officials of Babylonia.

steps.kashyaTarget: The version saying רבא was the father of רב מרי בר רחל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב had to validate him through his mother, so his father was not Jewish and could not be רבא.

steps.title: There may have been two men named מרי בר רחל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there may have been two people called מרי בר רחל: one whose father was a convert, and one whose father was רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps there were two people named מרי בר רחל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the side question by suggesting that two different people had the same name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man רב validated was the son of a non-Jewish father, and a different מרי בר רחל was the son of רבא. With two people, both facts can be true, and the 'father' version is no longer a problem.

phrases.aramaic: דִילְמָא תְּרֵי מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל הֲווֹ.
phrases.english: Perhaps there were two named Mari bar Rachel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִילְמָא תְּרֵי מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different people with the same name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was only one רב מרי בר רחל, so his father could not have been רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: There were two men with this name, so both versions can stand.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: one who drives his animal on שבת is fully exempt
steps.stepSummary: The teacher introduced in step 4 taught, in the name of רבי יוחנן, that a מחמר on שבת is פטור מכלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: He used to teach this teaching in the name of רבי יוחנן, saying the person is exempt. רבי יוחנן said: one who drives his animal on שבת is exempt from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: After the side discussion about who רב מרי בר רחל's father was, the גמרא returns to this teacher's actual opinion. He says a מחמר gets no punishment at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא suggested that a מחמר could get סקילה even without a חטאת. This teacher, quoting רבי יוחנן, says the opposite: there is no punishment of any kind. The next three steps will explain each punishment he is exempt from.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from any punishment at all

phrases.english: He would teach this teaching
phrases.notes: "He" is the teacher introduced in step 4, connected to רב מרי בר רחל.

phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, as exempt.
Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who drives his animal on Shabbat
phrases.notes: The word means "after" (behind) his animal: he walks behind it and drives it on.

phrases.english: is exempt from everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה מַתְנִי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לִפְטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side question about רב מרי בר רחל's family (steps 5-6) to the content of the opinion introduced in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מחמר on שבת is exempt from every punishment.

steps.title: No sin-offering when done by mistake
steps.stepSummary: There is no חטאת for a שוגג מחמר, because all of the Torah is compared to עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did it by mistake, he does not have to bring a חטאת, because the whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining פטור מכלום. The first punishment it removes is the חטאת for doing it by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah links the חטאת laws of every מצוה to the חטאת of עבודה זרה. In עבודה זרה you are only liable for an act you do yourself. When driving an animal, the animal carries the load and the person only drives it, so there is no חטאת.

phrases.english: By mistake, he is not liable to a sin-offering —
because the entire Torah was compared
to idolatry.
phrases.notes: The rule for idolatry is that you are liable only for an act done with your own body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first part of פטור מכלום from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שוגג מחמר does not bring a חטאת, based on the comparison of the Torah to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: No stoning when done on purpose
steps.stepSummary: There is no סקילה for a מזיד מחמר. The source teaches that only something that brings a חטאת by mistake brings סקילה on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did it on purpose, he is also not liable. We learned: one who breaks שבת with something that brings a חטאת by mistake brings סקילה on purpose. This implies that something which does not bring a חטאת by mistake does not bring סקילה on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now removes the second punishment, סקילה for doing it on purpose. It proves this from the same source that רבא quoted in his objection in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed there is no חטאת. This teacher reads the source to mean that סקילה only comes where there is a חטאת. So with no חטאת, there is no סקילה either. This is the exact inference that step 3 rejected, but this teacher accepts it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up. In step 3 the גמרא rejected this inference, and it said a מחמר could get סקילה without a חטאת. Here, the teacher quoting רבי יוחנן does use the inference. These are two different opinions, so there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: On purpose, he is also not liable —
as we learned: one who desecrates Shabbat
with a thing for whose mistaken doing one is liable to a sin-offering
and for whose purposeful doing, stoning.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין חַיָּיבִין עַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת —
phrases.english: This implies: where one is not liable to a sin-offering for its mistaken doing —
one is not liable to stoning for its purposeful doing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8. Since there is no חטאת, the source's inference removes סקילה too.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a מזיד מחמר is not stoned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The source (תנן) linking חטאת when done by mistake to סקילה when done on purpose, read by inference (הא).

steps.title: No lashes either, because this prohibition carries the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: There are no מלקות, because the לאו of שבת is a warning for מיתת בית דין, and such a לאו does not bring lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is also not liable for breaking a לאו. That לאו was given as a warning for a death penalty from the court, and for any לאו given as a warning for a death penalty from the court, we do not give lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the last possible punishment, lashes. That completes the explanation of פטור מכלום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that even without חטאת or סקילה, there is still a plain לאו here that brings lashes. But the שבת prohibition exists to warn about a death penalty. A לאו like that never brings lashes, even in a case where no death penalty is given.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning, the Torah's source for a prohibition
A death penalty given by the court

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן's tradition, a מחמר is פטור מכלום: no חטאת (all of the Torah is compared to עבודה זרה), no סקילה (no חטאת means no סקילה), and no מלקות (it is a לאו that warns of מיתת בית דין).
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "a לאו that is a warning for מיתת בית דין does not bring lashes" is a general principle used all over ש״ס, not only for שבת.

phrases.english: For a prohibition he is also not liable —
phrases.notes: This means lashes for breaking a לאו.

phrases.english: because it is a prohibition
that was given as a warning of a court death penalty,
and any prohibition that was given
as a warning of a court death penalty
one does not receive lashes for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the three-part explanation. After חטאת (step 8) and סקילה (step 9), it removes מלקות as well.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מחמר is free of all punishment: no חטאת, no סקילה, and no lashes, because the שבת לאו is a warning for מיתת בית דין.
